escalations.question: How should initial thinking selection behave when Pi reports that an available model does not support off?
escalations.context: REQ7 requires each thinking selector to start at off, including replacements, while REQ7 and AC13 require choices to exactly match Pi's supported thinking levels. In real interactive Pi 1.5.0, selecting the available openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol opened choices minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, highlighting minimal. There was no off choice. Pi's public getSupportedThinkingLevels filters levels explicitly mapped to null. The implementation correctly preserves those exact supported choices, but therefore cannot always start at off. This was discovered during the manual-only AC10 procedure, which remains incomplete. Automated tests and repository checks pass, including AC14's narrower case where the replacement model supports off.

options.description: Start at off when supported; otherwise start at Pi's first supported thinking level.
options.consequences: Preserves the complete available model catalog and exact supported choices. Changes the unconditional off-start requirement and related human guidance.
options.nextStep: Revise and approve the contract through Maestro, then resume builder verification and complete manual AC10.

options.description: Limit setup model choices to available models whose supported thinking levels include off.
options.consequences: Preserves an unconditional off starting choice but excludes otherwise available models, including the observed gpt-6.1-sol. Changes model-catalog selection requirements and requires owner-approved filtering behavior.
options.nextStep: Revise and approve the model eligibility contract through Maestro, then implement the approved filter and repeat all acceptance proofs.

recommendation.reason: The real Pi model catalog contains reasoning models without off. Using Pi's first supported level for those models preserves valid capability choices without excluding available models or inventing unsupported thinking levels.

notes: Reference this question as B1/E1. No unsupported off choice was injected and no model-catalog filtering was added.

resolution.decision: Revise REQ7 and AC14 so each thinking selector always starts at the first supported thinking level in the order returned by Pi, for both initial selections and replacements. Do not give off any preference, even when it is supported.
resolution.reason: The owner explicitly chose Pi's supported-level ordering as the sole rule for the initial thinking selection, without a special case for off.
